To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the genetic diversity of small populations is not necessarily correlated with the size of the population and (2) small population size and genetic diversity are not the only factors contributing to species persistence.

the most important factors influencing the persistence of small populations are: (i) population size and genetic diversity; (ii) demographic stochasticity; (iii) genetic inbreeding; (iv) genetic adaptation; and (v) environmental stochasticity.

(1) population genetic diversity and genetic structure are not always good predictors of population viability, (2) genetic diversity is not necessarily a good indicator of evolutionary potential, (3) the best way to manage a population is to understand its ecology and behavior, and (4) the best way forward is to implement a National Center for Population Biology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the genetic and ecological factors that influence population viability and evolutionary potential.
the genetic consequences of anthropogenic impacts and how to use genetics and genomics to inform management and policy decisions.
understanding the genetic and demographic processes that influence the persistence of species, particularly those that have experienced population declines.
